tagline: Down the Colorado's gorge to the potash ponds.
intro: Potash Road turns off US 191 just north of Moab, and after 2.7 miles it enters the deep gorge of the Colorado River, following the north bank downstream under reddish-orange sandstone cliffs. Near the four-mile mark climbers work the walls of the stretch called Wall Street. Past Jug Handle Arch the canyon widens, and the sheer cliffs below Dead Horse Point show in the distance.

The road was built in 1962 and 1963 to serve a potash mine, the first piece of a longer route up to Dead Horse Point that was never finished. At the mine, potash is flushed from underground tunnels with water, and the water is left to evaporate in ponds.

moments.title: Petroglyph panels
moments.text: At mile 5.1 several panels of petroglyphs show on the cliffs beside the highway, with marked pull-offs across the road.

moments.title: Dinosaur tracks
moments.text: From the Poison Spider trailhead at mile 5.9 a short trail leads to dinosaur tracks and more rock art.

moments.title: Corona Arch
moments.text: A 1.5-mile trail leads to an arch with an opening 140 by 105 feet, also known as Little Rainbow for its likeness to Rainbow Bridge at Lake Powell.

practical: The pavement ends at the potash mine. Beyond it a dirt road continues toward Canyonlands National Park for high-clearance vehicles.

sources.label: Discover Moab, Potash-Lower Colorado River Scenic Byway (U-279)
